grades.quote: The single block can be the commit record in a write-ahead log, as I discussed in Section 5.4.
grades.reason: Explains why a crash during multi-block metadata updates leaves a filesystem inconsistent and says a write-ahead log commit record is one integrity strategy. The passage cuts off before it explains how the log is used for recovery, so it gives only background.

grades.quote: Even if the system crashes and restarts, the transaction manager will see its own commitment log record and go forward with phase two.
grades.reason: Describes how commit records and redo/undo logs let a transaction be completed or rolled back after a crash, in two-phase commit. It is not about filesystems or write-ahead logging for filesystem updates, so it is only loosely related.
